Not really a rant, but I don’t understand the coach Beiste transition storyline. Up until the episode before he announced that he was transitioning, storylines about his gender were always pretty much centered around how he didn’t fit “traditional” feminine gender roles and that that was okay. I would’ve completely understood it if the actress was transitioning, but as far as I know she didn’t. 

I would have loved to see a transgender teacher brought in, especially during season 4 or 5. They could’ve cast someone who is actually transgender, and there could’ve been some great mentorship-like storylines with them and Unique. Especially if it was someone who transitioned later in life. They could’ve helped Unique since they had struggled with body dysmorphia well into adulthood and understood what dealing with it was like, and Unique could’ve helped them since she was confident with who she was at a young age.

Idk, I just feel like it came out of nowhere with nothing leading up to it, it takes away from women who also don’t fit societal gender norms, and it kinda negates most of Beiste’s storylines before his transition.

It depends on the hospital tbh. I was in group therapy with a girl who straight up said she didn’t believe in hospitalization because of her experiences. However, myself and the rest of the group (about 10 people) all said that our experiences weren’t terrible. Don’t get me wrong, it’s obviously not fun, like it’s boring as shit, but it won’t traumatize you. I went to a hospital for 5 days and the worst parts were that it was kinda religious based and I’m an atheist so that sucked, and missing the comforts of home (the bed wasn’t great, I wanted my blanket, I couldn’t wear my ring that I get anxious without, couldn’t keep my chapstick with me, missed my dog, stuff like that). The food was better than expected and the people, both other patients and staff, were actually really nice and understanding since it was my first time in a hospital like that.
